reading.title: Why We Buy Things We Don't Need
reading.intro_zh: 拓展话题不复述帽店争论，而是聚焦冲动消费背后的心理学：为什么我们会买下根本不需要的东西。本文改写自一篇发表于《Frontiers in Psychology》、由美国国立医学图书馆 (NCBI/PMC) 收录的同行评议论文。

source.title: Factors Affecting Impulse Buying Behavior of Consumers
source.publisher: Frontiers in Psychology (NCBI/PMC, U.S. National Library of Medicine)

passage: Almost everyone has, at some point, walked into a shop intending to buy nothing and walked out carrying a bag. Researchers call this impulse buying, and it is far more common than most shoppers would willingly admit. By some estimates, between forty and eighty percent of all purchases are made on impulse rather than according to any plan. An impulse purchase is not simply something you forgot to put on your list; it is driven by a sudden, powerful emotional urge that briefly overrides the rational part of the mind responsible for weighing cost against genuine need.

Psychologists who study the phenomenon argue that these urges rarely come from nowhere. People are far more vulnerable when their mood is low, their self-control is depleted, or their anxiety is running high, because a quick purchase can momentarily relieve those uncomfortable feelings. Retailers, meanwhile, have refined an environment engineered to encourage exactly this reaction. Bright displays, carefully arranged shelves, pleasant background music, appealing scents, and limited-time discounts all stimulate the senses before logical judgement has time to intervene. Notably, physical stores provoke considerably more unplanned spending than online ones, partly because a screen cannot reproduce the same rich sensory experience.

Yet the research offers a measure of reassurance. Buying habits are shaped by a tangle of emotional, social, and cultural influences rather than by any single weakness, which means no one is helplessly programmed to overspend. Understanding the psychological levers that retailers pull is itself a form of defence: a shopper who recognises the trick is better placed to pause, question the urge, and decide whether the desire reflects a real need or merely a passing feeling.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Online shopping has completely replaced shopping in physical stores.
Retailers should be legally forbidden from using music and scents.
Impulse buying is a common, psychologically driven behaviour that shoppers can learn to resist.
People who buy on impulse always regret their purchases afterwards.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文先说明冲动消费很普遍、由心理冲动驱动，再说零售环境如何刺激它，最后指出了解这些机制就能更好地抵御，因此主旨是 C。

questions.question: According to the passage, what proportion of purchases are estimated to be made on impulse?
options: Between forty and eighty percent.
Exactly half of all purchases.
Fewer than a quarter of purchases.
Nearly every purchase people make.
questions.explanation_zh: 第一段明确说 between forty and eighty percent of all purchases are made on impulse，所以是 40% 到 80%。

questions.question: Why does the passage say people are more vulnerable to impulse buying?
options: Because shops are usually too crowded to think clearly.
Because a quick purchase can briefly relieve low mood, weak self-control, or anxiety.
Because most people genuinely need the items they buy.
Because online stores offer richer sensory experiences than physical ones.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段说当人情绪低落、自控力耗尽或焦虑时更脆弱，因为快速购买能暂时缓解这些不适感，故选 B。

questions.question: What can be inferred from the passage about resisting impulse buying?
options: It is impossible once a person enters a store.
It depends only on how much money someone earns.
It requires shopping exclusively online.
Awareness of retailers' tactics makes a shopper more able to resist.
questions.explanation_zh: 结尾说了解零售商的心理手法本身就是一种防御，认出套路的人更容易停下来质疑冲动，可推断出 D。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "overrides" ("briefly overrides the rational part of the mind") most nearly means
options: carefully strengthens.
temporarily overpowers and sets aside.
politely requests permission from.
permanently destroys.
questions.explanation_zh: overrides 在文中指冲动暂时压过、盖过理性的部分，让理性失去作用，所以最接近 B（暂时压制并搁置）。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 41 的五个购物争论句式提升到 B2+：用 Do you call that...? 写带分析意味的尖锐反问，用 needn't be so... 提醒对方收敛态度，用 mustn't 写消费自控的规则，用 regretted saying... 写脱口而出后的即时懊悔，再用 needn't have said... 评价那句本可不说的话；尽量放进更抽象、更成人化的语境。

patterns.title: Do you call that ...?
patterns.source: Do you call that a hat?
patterns.focus_zh: 这是一个尖锐的反问，意思不是认真询问名称，而是带着批评或讽刺；写作时要知道它可能会伤人。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：用 Do you call that...? 对某个被吹捧的方案、产品或作品提出带分析意味的尖锐质疑，并说明它真正欠缺什么。
patterns.sample: Do you call that a marketing strategy when the entire campaign relies on tricking tired shoppers into spending impulsively?
patterns.tip_zh: 这个句式语气很重，适合分析故事冲突；真实交流中常常需要换成更礼貌的表达。

patterns.title: needn't be so ...
patterns.source: You needn't be so rude about it.
patterns.focus_zh: needn't be so... 表示“没必要这么……”，常用来提醒对方降低语气或态度。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人提醒对方在抽象或正式的情境里（如评价他人的计划、品味或决定）不必那么挑剔、轻蔑或焦虑。
patterns.sample: You needn't be so dismissive of her budget plan simply because it requires more discipline than you are comfortable with.
patterns.tip_zh: needn't 后面接动词原形 be；so 后面放形容词，如 rude, worried, nervous, direct。

patterns.title: mustn't buy things we don't need
patterns.source: We mustn't buy things we don't need.
patterns.focus_zh: mustn't 表示比较强的禁止或规则，用在花钱场景里像是在提醒自己要自控。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写一个人或一个家庭即使面对限时折扣或新奇外观，也不应为了一时的满足感而买下不需要的东西。
patterns.sample: However tempting the limited-time discounts may appear, we mustn't buy things we don't need merely to chase a fleeting feeling of satisfaction.
patterns.tip_zh: mustn't 比 don't need to 更强，像给自己立一条规则。

patterns.title: regretted saying ...
patterns.source: I regretted saying it almost at once.
patterns.focus_zh: regretted saying... 写“说出口之后后悔”，后面常接 it, that, 或具体说过的话。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人在社交或正式场合说了一句太直接、太尖刻的话，话音未落便后悔，并点出造成的后果。
patterns.sample: She regretted saying that the gift looked cheap, because the careless remark embarrassed everyone gathered around the table.
patterns.tip_zh: regretted 后面接动名词 saying；as soon as 可以写出“立刻后悔”的节奏。

patterns.title: needn't have said ...
patterns.focus_zh: needn't have said... 表示“你已经说了，但那句话本来没必要”，常带一点责备或提醒。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人指出别人刚才那句话本可以不说，尤其是在众人面前让某人难堪或贬低了他人的喜好时。
patterns.sample: You needn't have said that his collection was a waste of money in front of the very friends who had admired it.
patterns.tip_zh: needn't have done 专门评价已经发生的过去动作：做了，但其实没必要做。
